title: Representing Higher-Order Networks: A Survey of Graph-Based Frameworks
summary: Many real-world phenomena can be naturally represented using graphs and networks. Classical graph models, however, are generally restricted to pairwise interactions and may therefore be insufficient for capturing the richer structural relationships encountered in practical systems. Higher-order graph formalisms extend the classical framework by incorporating multiway, hierarchical, temporal, multilayer, recursive, and tensor-based interactions, thereby enabling more expressive representations of complex systems.
